heading: INT. COACHING INN - COMMON ROOM - NIGHT - 1817

units.text: INT. COACHING INN - COMMON ROOM - NIGHT - 1817
A low room, black beams, a hearth coughing smoke.
Rain beats the shutters.
A single tallow candle gutters on a long table scarred with a century of knives.
INNKEEPER SILAS PRYCE (50s, bald, apron stiff with grease) wipes the same tankard he has wiped for an hour.
He is a man who has learned to be furniture.
At the far end, a WOMAN IN A DRIPPING TRAVELLING CLOAK (30s, pale, gloves the colour of wet slate) sits very upright, her hands folded.
She has not removed her bonnet.
Rain runs from its ribbons onto her collar.
By the fire, a YOUNG SOLDIER (20s, red coat unbuttoned, one boot off) toasts his stockinged foot and does not look at either of them.
Last coach was due at nine. Roads are drowned between here and Dunstable. Nobody leaves tonight.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: The soldier grunts.
The woman does not move.
Ma'am, will you be wanting a room?
units.name: SILAS

units.text: I will want to sit.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: Sit as long as you please, then.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: He goes back to the tankard.
The fire pops.
A log collapses.
God rot this country. God rot these roads.
units.name: YOUNG SOLDIER

units.text: The stranger turns her head, slowly, toward him.
Studies the unbuttoned coat.
The bare foot.
You are far from your regiment, sir.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: I'm where I'm sent.
units.name: YOUNG SOLDIER

units.text: By whom?
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: He does not answer.
His heel rubs the hearthstone, up and down.
Leave the lad be, ma'am. He's had a hard road.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: We all have. It is why we are here.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: She rises.
The chair legs scrape.
She crosses the room at a measured pace and stops by the table, close enough to the candle that her face is lit from below for the first time: a long jaw, grey eyes, a scar that bisects one eyebrow.
Landlord. How many guests do you keep?
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: Three tonight, now. Yourself, the lad, and me.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: Four, I think. Counting the one in the cellar.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: Silas's tankard stops.
The cloth hangs in his hand.
There's none in my cellar.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: Captain Hale.
units.name: YOUNG SOLDIER

units.text: The stranger looks at him.
Something in her face releases, like a hand opening.
You know me, then.
units.name: HALE

units.text: Everyone knows you. They said you'd hanged.
units.name: YOUNG SOLDIER

units.text: They said that of my husband.
units.name: HALE

units.text: Silas sets the tankard down at last.
Lord. Lord, forgive an old fool.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: Nobody will be hurt. I have come for what is in the cellar, and then I shall go back into the rain.
units.name: HALE

units.text: The soldier shakes his head.
He reaches for the boot he has taken off, and for the sword beside it.
I can't let you.
units.name: YOUNG SOLDIER

units.text: No. I know. That is why I wore the gloves.
units.name: HALE

units.text: She raises her hands.
The wet slate gloves are stitched, at the knuckles, with something small and bright.
The candle flares.
The shutters bang open on the storm.
SMASH CUT TO BLACK.
